name: Trax
classification_notes: A chunky, rounded-terminal display sans referencing vinyl-label and disco-era lettering, placing it in the display sans category.
summary: A chunky, rounded display sans built as a variable font, styled after disco and house-era record labels.
description: Trax is a bold, rounded sans-serif with a variable weight axis and matching italic, its thick strokes and soft terminals recalling vintage vinyl label and record-sleeve lettering.
foundry_blurb: dito-typo present Trax through a live specimen built around house and disco music references, offered as a variable font with a matching italic.

name: Gutach
classification_notes: A heavy serif with rounded ball terminals evoking German heritage signage, placing it in the slab-leaning serif category.
summary: A heavy, ball-terminal serif named after a Black Forest valley, styled after German heritage signage.
description: Gutach is a bold serif with rounded ball terminals and a variable weight axis running from Book to Black, its specimen copy leaning into Black Forest place names and heritage engraving.
foundry_blurb: dito-typo present Gutach as a variable serif family named for the Gutach valley in the Black Forest, running from Book through to Black.

name: Rutor Steel
classification_notes: Slotted, geometric letterforms inspired by CNC milling precision place Rutor Steel in the display category rather than a conventional text serif or sans.
summary: A slotted, geometric display face inspired by the precision of a CNC milling machine, in three weights and a variable cut.
description: Rutor Steel is one half of the two-part Rutor project, built around interrupted, slotted strokes that read as precision-machined rather than drawn. Three weights run from Regular to Black, with a variable font available alongside.
foundry_blurb: dito-typo describe the two Rutor families, Steel and Stone, as inspired by the chiseled Art Nouveau inscriptions of Darmstadt's Mathildenhöhe and by the precision and aesthetics of a CNC milling machine.

name: Rutor Stone
classification_notes: Organic, whiplash curves cut into blocky letterforms reference Art Nouveau inscriptions, placing Rutor Stone in the display category.
summary: An Art Nouveau-inspired display face with organic, whiplash curves cut into solid letterforms, referencing Darmstadt's Mathildenhöhe.
description: Rutor Stone is the organic-curved sibling to Rutor Steel, drawing on the chiseled Art Nouveau inscriptions of Darmstadt's Mathildenhöhe artist colony. Three weights run from Regular to Black.
foundry_blurb: dito-typo describe the two Rutor families, Steel and Stone, as inspired by the chiseled Art Nouveau inscriptions of Darmstadt's Mathildenhöhe and by the precision and aesthetics of a CNC milling machine.
